clue.text: Vaulting ambition involves a tricky move

indicators.note: involves says the clue words hold the answer within their letters, straddling the word break

explanation.surface: Leaping ambition leads someone into a risky manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening sacrificing material for advantage, and so any calculated ploy, is called this.

clue.text: Rugby's first to be entertained by an elderly Victorian headmaster

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word Rugby's

parts.note: elderly means old

explanation.surface: A pupil at Rugby School is first in line to be received by an old Victorian head.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arnold was the famous headmaster of Rugby School, a leading English public school, in the 1830s.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arnold, reforming head of Rugby School in the Victorian era, is the man named.

clue.text: Stroke an insect

definitions.meaning: a swimming style with both arms swung over together
a winged creature with broad, often colourful wings

explanation.definitionFit: Both a swimming stroke and a colourful flying insect share this name.

clue.text: Display outrageous paintings when turning up in restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to air something is to display it
OTT is short for over the top, meaning outrageous
paintings are art

explanation.surface: Garish pictures put on show in an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AIROTTART as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian trattoria is a small, informal restaurant serving simple food.

clue.text: Picture making one wise after sin? Not entirely

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the first one
not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins
I is the Roman numeral for one
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Someone imagines becoming wise once they have sinned, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine or visualise it in the mind.

clue.text: "What's in orbit?" I shout aloud

indicators.note: aloud says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: I shout can be expressed as I bawl

explanation.surface: Someone yells a question about what circles in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbit' suggests space, but it is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit is the bony socket of the skull, and the eye sits inside it.

clue.text: Five Gaelic poems

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Five poems written in the Gaelic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry in general, or a set of poems, is called verse.

clue.text: Opening letters from Dumas to Maupassant

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Early correspondence between two great French novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a stoma is a small pore or mouth-like aperture in a leaf or body.

clue.text: Good Scots, say, holding party for blind leader

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: e.g. means for example, or say
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Good Scottish people throw a party for a leader who cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained dog leads a sightless person safely around obstacles.

clue.text: Start with what the setter did in 4?

parts.note: taken as written
4 down is a restaurant, referred to here as it
the setter speaks of themself as I
in a restaurant what one did is ate

explanation.surface: A question about beginning with what the compiler did in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter dined in the restaurant of 4 down: IN IT, I ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to begin or set something going.

clue.text: 25 that is for novice

parts.note: 25 across is fleece, meaning to swindle, which is also rook

explanation.surface: Swindle someone, that is, a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a beginner or recruit new to a job.

clue.text: Customer is right in court

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a lien is a legal right over another's property

explanation.surface: A customer is proved correct in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services, a customer.

clue.text: Area due for reunification accepting new chancellor

reunification brings the letters together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A region awaiting reunification welcomes a new head of government, as Germany did.
explanation.walkthrough: Konrad Adenauer was the first chancellor of West Germany; 'reunification' fits the German surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Konrad Adenauer served as West Germany's first post-war chancellor.

clue.text: Niece not even born

indicators.note: not even says to take the odd-numbered letters only

explanation.surface: A niece who is not yet even born.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Poor law or new folk song? Possibly

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are badly arranged and must be put right

explanation.surface: A question about whether the old Poor Law could inspire a new folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a well-known popular song title, and the phrase itself means perhaps.

clue.text: Airy advance with weapon over battle zone

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier pieces above the next

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
the front is where the fighting takes place

explanation.surface: Troops push forward with weapons across a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: In weather, a boundary of advancing mild air is named this.

clue.text: Untamed rebel like aggressive insect

indicators.note: untamed suggests the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild rebel behaves like a fierce insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Africanised honeybee, notoriously quick to swarm and sting, has this nickname.

clue.text: Pretty Flamingo's last in West Ham ground

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
ground means the letters are crushed and reshaped
last picks the final letter of the word Flamingo's

explanation.surface: Pretty Flamingo, a 1960s pop hit, played last at West Ham's football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty Flamingo' reads as a song title, but 'Pretty' is the definition. West Ham is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty, as in pretty good, means fairly or to some degree.

clue.text: Something fishy all heard at the beginning? Gosh!

indicators.note: at the beginning puts that piece at the front of the answer
heard says a word is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: wholly means all, entirely
a mackerel is a fish

explanation.surface: A suspicious tale everyone heard right at the start, and someone exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an exclamation of surprise, much like gosh or wow.

clue.text: Clean head of hair

definitions.meaning: to clean a floor with a wet swab
a thick, untidy shock of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Both a floor-cleaning tool's action and a shaggy mass of hair share the word.

clue.text: Material for nails supplied by a tinker

indicators.note: supplied hints at the letters being made supple and bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: Stuff for nails provided by a travelling mender.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the protein that forms fingernails, hair and horn.

clue.text: Heartless cavalier in spotted cloak

parts.note: spotted means seen

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of cavalier are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: An unfeeling Royalist gentleman wearing a spotted cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to hide or conceal, as a cloak does.

clue.text: Terribly hard piece without a crack

clue.text: Publication for children

explanation.definitionFit: It means both an edition of a periodical and one's offspring.

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of London

clue.text: Garment to take to the cleaners

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a soft warm jacket and a verb meaning to swindle.

clue.text: Mad Hatter? No, cricketer

clue.text: You need empty words on last page
